title: Country brass bands and funerals around Paul Rocher
summary: Miller says a country band led by Paul Rocher played the same marches, hymns and jump-back music as New Orleans bands.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: What kind of funerals did they have out in the country? What kind of brass band music is what I'm getting at.

I played, well, I was a young kid then, but I couldn't say I played with a fella named Paul Rocher. Out in Louisiana, to call him. And he had about a good band. He had about a good band as they had down here. Brass band. He had some real good musicians. Did they play the same kind of music? Yeah, they played the same kind of marches and everything they played there.
Did they play hymns and tenorals?

Yeah, hymns. Of course, they wasn't walking on the pavement, they weren't in the dusty road, but they played good music. They turned out just like they did to other people. They just lay off and go to the field.
Did they play the same kind of coming back music?

Yeah. Jump back playing the didn't even ramble or something like that, you know. Well, they got the idea from you, you know. Somebody come in and isn't how to do it. You can rather than do the same thing.
